title: Statistical assessment and evidence grading

grade_scale.note: E0-E4 are internal computational evidence grades defined for this project; they are not an established neuroscience standard. The Phase 4H protocol used a different E0-E4 wording, so the definitions below are the ones applied in this report.

definitions.E0: Infrastructure: data integrity, graph construction, deterministic execution and software validation.
definitions.E1: Computational activity: the model produces reproducible neural activity under stated assumptions.
definitions.E2: Population-level sensitivity: activity changes reproducibly with controlled inputs or perturbations.
definitions.E3: Functional pathway evidence: input-dependent activity propagates through relevant intermediate populations and reaches the intended output population.
definitions.E4: Validated behavioural evidence: controlled learning and behavioural performance, supported by appropriate independent validation.

limitations: The five families are not equally matched to C; family E is an approximation and the realised standardised differences are reported.

A difference from these controls is not evidence of biological motor control; the motor response is a simulated decoder output.
Zero noise means no spontaneous activity; background/noise conditions are outside 4H.1.
Phase 4G condition C was selected on motor-synapse rank, so the reference lies at the extreme tail of families A-E by construction.

limitations: Ranked rules are deterministic and run once, so they carry no sampling uncertainty; only random rules quantify variability.
Degree is a structural property of the threshold-5 graph; no biological meaning is assigned to in-, out- or combined degree.
The eligible pool is fixed by the Phase 4F verified-excitatory policy; unverified or inhibitory neurons are outside this surface.
The JUMP null model reuses motor spike counts from one run and tests pool size and identity, not biological recruitment.
A single pre-registered confirmatory comparison is made at size 64; the rest of the surface is exploratory and not corrected.

limitations: No transform is established as the correct model of synaptic strength.
The result is conditional on the fixed Phase 4G condition C group.
A JUMP decoder label is not a biological jump command.
Sign policies are annotation assumptions, not measured biology.
W7 is a labelled approximation of count/post_count; the dataset family is unavailable.
The 10 repeats are deterministic and provide no inferential replication; permutation tests are numerical equivalence checks.
The three streams are non-overlapping segments of one recording group, not independent recordings.
Event timestamps are synthesized at 30 fps because the images carry no timestamps; ordering and gaps come from the unchanged Phase 3B pipeline.
Only lifecycle events carrying feature values drive current; the archived replay exposes events, not per-frame GameState features, so no held per-frame state is used.
The mapping from a game feature to a BANC annotation pool is a labelled hypothesis or convention, not a measured sensory pathway.
No confirmatory p-value is claimed across the three non-independent streams; evidence level E4 is not claimed.
A motor spike or decoder label is not a biological motor command.

Q1_decoder_deterministic.question: Is the motor decoder deterministic?
Q1_decoder_deterministic.caveat: Determinism is a software property, not biological reproducibility.

Q2_robust_to_random_draws.question: Is the decoder output robust to random control draws?

Q2_robust_to_random_draws.caveat: The p-value is at the floor of the 100-draw design; the controls are matched approximations, not a random sample of all neurons.

Q4_stable_across_weight_transformations.question: Is the output stable across weight transformations?

s2_equals_s0.note: S2 retains unknown-sign edges with zero weight, which is numerically identical to excluding them; any difference would be a bug, not a scientific result

w4_equals_w1.note: power exponent 1.0 with scale 0.5 and cap 300 is the same transform as linear with scale 0.5 and cap 300

cap_saturation.interpretation: the W0 cap binds for an edge whose structural count reaches the threshold; above it W0 and W5 differ only by the cap

Q4_stable_across_weight_transformations.caveat: JUMP is present only for W0/W5/W6 at nominal drive; W1-W4/W7 produce no JUMP. Matched-amplitude D1 restores JUMP for W1-W6, so the effect is amplitude- as well as transform-dependent.

Q5_sensory_downstream_propagation.question: Does sensory stimulation produce downstream propagation?
Q5_sensory_downstream_propagation.caveat: 662 signed edges produced 9,499 signed spike-to-edge transmissions, but no first-hop spike. Structural connectivity does not imply effective propagation.

Q6_actual_vs_shuffled.question: Does actual sensory-event structure produce distinguishable responses compared with shuffled controls?
Q6_actual_vs_shuffled.caveat: The difference is confined to stimulated spike totals; it has no downstream or decoder consequence and changes sign across the three streams. E2/E3 are not awarded.

Q7_activity_reaches_descending_and_motor.question: Does activity reach descending and motor populations?
Q7_activity_reaches_descending_and_motor.caveat: Four motor neurons are structurally reachable at two signed hops; none receives current because the first hop does not fire.

Q8_assumption_dependence.question: Are apparent effects dependent on specific model assumptions?
Q8_assumption_dependence.caveat: The direction of the 4G result is not invariant to the weight transform or sign policy; the sensory round-trip is additionally conditional on the annotation mapping.

claims.claim: Sensory stimulation propagates beyond the directly stimulated neurons to first-hop and later populations.
claims.reason: No non-stimulated neuron spiked. Synaptic current reached 473 of 607 downstream first-hop targets, but the closest neuron remained 6.926 mV below threshold. E3 is not awarded.

claims.claim: Actual sensory-event structure produces a distinguishable propagated downstream response compared with shuffled controls.
claims.reason: A small difference exists in stimulated spike totals, but there is no propagated or decoder-level difference; the sign of the B-versus-C difference is also mixed across streams. E2/E3 are not awarded.

claims.claim: Sensory activity reaches descending neurons and motor neurons.
claims.reason: 4 motor neurons are structurally two signed hops from the stimulated group, but none receives current or spikes. E3 is not awarded.

claims.claim: A LEFT, RIGHT or JUMP decoder output is a validated biological motor command or behavioural action.
claims.reason: E4 requires controlled behavioural learning and independent validation; neither exists.

claims.claim: The game-feature-to-BANC mapping is a measured visual or sensory pathway.
claims.reason: The mapping is a computational convention, not a measured pathway.

claims.claim: The reported effects are invariant to the main model assumptions (weight transform, sign policy, drive, mapping).
claims.reason: At nominal drive JUMP is present only for ['D0_W0_S0', 'D0_W0_S2', 'D0_W5_S0', 'D0_W6_S0'] and absent elsewhere; the silent configurations are ['D0_W0_S3', 'D0_W0_S4', 'D0_W2_S0', 'D0_W2_S1', 'D0_W3_S0', 'D0_W3_S1', 'D0_W7_S0']. E2 sensitivity is supported, but assumption-invariance is not.

strongest_supported_conclusion: Under the fixed verified-only sign policy and W0 weight transform, a 64-neuron VNC-intrinsic group selected on motor-synapse rank produces a reproducible simulated motor/JUMP decoder output that is distinguishable from five matched random-control families (E2). The output is strongly dependent on weight transform, sign policy and drive amplitude. Sensory stimulation at the tested 200 pA per-feature drive produces spikes only in the stimulated sensory neurons; synaptic current reaches first-hop targets but does not bring any of them to threshold, so there is no propagation to descending or motor populations and no E3 functional-pathway evidence.
unsupported_claims: That sensory events drive descending or motor-neuron activity in this model.
That actual event structure produces a distinguishable propagated response compared with shuffled controls.
That 662 signed outgoing edges imply effective downstream activation.
That a LEFT, RIGHT or JUMP decoder label is a biological motor command or observed behaviour.
That the game-feature-to-BANC mapping is a measured visual pathway.
That the Phase 4G JUMP result is invariant to weight transform or sign policy.
That the model provides E3 functional-pathway evidence or E4 behavioural evidence.
That stationary or constant-charge drive is equivalent to the actual event sequence.
remaining_uncertainties: Structural connectivity is not physiological connectivity: sign, weight and delay are model priors.
44.5% of threshold-5 edges carry a verified transmitter sign; the rest are excluded and may change propagation.
Synaptic weights are monotone transforms of structural synapse counts, not measured conductances.
The 232-neuron sensory mapping is an annotation-defined hypothesis, not a measured receptive-field map.
BANC is one specimen and one dataset export; annotation completeness and proofreading are limited.
Event timestamps are synthesized at 30 fps because the source images carry no timestamps.
No validated biological labels exist for LEFT, RIGHT or JUMP.
The absence of propagation at 200 pA does not prove that the network cannot propagate at other drives or weights.
The three streams are non-overlapping segments of one recording group, not independent recordings.
A motor-neuron spike in the simulator is not a validated motor command or behaviour.

recommended_next_experiment.title: Pre-registered sensory-drive threshold and propagation calibration
recommended_next_experiment.rationale: The current experiment establishes that 200 pA per-feature pulses reach first-hop membranes but remain subthreshold. The next step is to estimate the input level at which the first hop crosses threshold, not to search for a setting that produces motor activity.
design: Pre-register a fixed geometric drive series (for example 200, 400, 800, 1200 pA per feature) with all seven conditions A-G on all three streams.
Record the same first-hop, second-hop, descending and motor diagnostics with hash-verified replays.
Report every cell, including silent cells; do not select a drive after observing motor output.
Add a direct first-hop current-injection positive control to verify that first-hop neurons can spike under the model.
Add a single-first-hop-spike test to measure whether one first-hop spike produces any second-hop current or spike.
Repeat the analysis on an independent recording or a second specimen before any E3/E4 claim.
recommended_next_experiment.decision_rule: The experiment succeeds if it estimates a threshold and reports it, regardless of whether motor activity appears.

overall_verdict.rationale: All 27 Phase 4H.4 runs completed with verified configuration, determinism and integrity. Phase 4H.1-4H.4 support E0-E2 claims. The sensory round-trip is reproducibly motor-silent and produces no E3 pathway evidence. This is a controlled negative result, not an execution failure.

limitations: Evidence grades are project-specific and were assigned after the results were known.
The 4H.1 p-values are at the minimum attainable value for 100 control draws.
Condition C was selected on the same motor-synapse rank used in the control comparison.
The weight and sign studies are deterministic sweeps, not independent biological replicates.
The sensory streams are non-independent segments of one recording.
No claim about behaviour, perception or biological motor control is supported.
